# Elsewhere — Idle RPG in Claude Code

> **Unbounded input, entering a bounded deterministic reality engine — and an AI beside
> you that has to narrate the result and live with it exactly like you do.** That is the
> whole architecture and the whole pitch.
>
> An idle RPG that runs inside Claude Code in real time. Three neighbouring factions
> each pursue an agenda on ten-segment clocks that advance whether the player is
> present or not. The player has one lookout and five standing orders. A Python
> engine decides every outcome with a seeded RNG and writes it to an append-only
> ledger; the language model reads that ledger and narrates it, and is never
> permitted to decide an outcome. Players may also type arbitrary freeform schemes,
> which are translated into costs and modifiers and then resolved by the same engine.
> When a world ends, the model writes a narrative chronicle from the ledger,
> including everything the player could not see during play.

Site: https://netmobster.github.io/elsewhere-idle-cc/
Repository: https://github.com/netmobster/elsewhere-idle-cc
Genesis: https://seren-dm.lovable.app/ (SEREN — the engine, ledger and roll system)

## See it played

- [demo.html](https://netmobster.github.io/elsewhere-idle-cc/demo.html): One complete
  game, eight in-world days, scene by scene — the chat, the board and the picker in
  frame together. Every player line is verbatim and every roll is taken from the
  engine's ledger. The fastest way to understand what this actually is.

## Core design

- [README.md](README.md): The complete overview — mechanics, the four surfaces, the
  determinism position, install, balance results, and the SEREN lineage.
- [PRD-TRD.md](PRD-TRD.md): Product and technical specification. Tick model, clock
  advance formula, order resolution ladder, action catalogue, fog-of-war contract,
  fitness criteria.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): The shipping record — what changed in each release,
  with the balance numbers as they stood at the time. Read this before citing any
  figure from the README; the balance was re-measured after the settle rule changed.
- [NOTES.md](NOTES.md): The honest build log. Every iteration including the failed
  ones, two determinism bugs, two fog leaks, and the balance measurements that were
  invalidated and re-run.

## Source

- [engine.py](engine.py): Authoritative. Seeded per-tick RNG derived from
  `(seed, absolute tick)` and nothing else. Clock advance, raids, order resolution,
  compounding interest, mega projects with a ten-entry mutation table, and the
  improvise path used for freeform player requests.
- [render.py](render.py): Renders the board. Enforces the fog contract — never emits
  a `true` fact, renders `known`/`suspected`/`false` identically, withholds ledger
  clock rows for unwatched factions.
- [epilogue.py](epilogue.py): Runs once when a world settles. Lifts the fog, scores
  the run, renders the badge and the chronicle.
- [sim.py](sim.py): Scripted players (attentive, hoarder, erratic, absentee) for
  fast-forward testing.
- [bench.py](bench.py): Six fitness criteria across N world seeds. Exits non-zero on
  failure.

## For agents operating this project

The load-bearing rule, inherited from SEREN, is that **the model narrates a result it
did not choose**. Every outcome exists in the ledger before any text is written about
it. A narrator that decides outcomes cannot be surprised by a roll, and the player
can tell. Do not resolve anything in prose.

Determinism is enforced, not assumed. Per-tick RNG must derive from `(seed, tick)`
only — never wall-clock time, never `hash()` (Python salts string hashing per
process), never dict or list ordering. Two separate bugs of this class shipped
during development and are documented in NOTES.md.

The fog contract is not cosmetic. If a `true` fact, an unwatched clock value, or a
marker distinguishing a false belief from a true one reaches the player, the fog is
decoration and the game's central tension is gone.
